newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Egypt bans Irish beef on BSE worries - minister.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bans Irish beef on BSE worries - minister.

text.p: Egypt has reimposed a ban on live Irish cattle imports because of concern in Cairo about the BSE scare, Agriculture Minister Ivan Yates said on Tuesday.
Yates said a decree signed by the Egyptian authorities was also banning live cattle imports from France and Portugal as well as beef imports from Britain and Switzerland.
Egypt clamped a ban on Irish beef imports last year at the height of a Europe-wide scare about so-called Mad Cow disease and its links to a fatal illness in humans.
But the ban was dropped after contacts between Irish Prime MInister John Bruton and Egytian President Hosni Mubarak.
The new sanctions will last for six months and then be reviewed by the Egyptian authorities, Yates said.
Cairo's concern apparently follows a rise in the number of confirmed BSE cases in several Irish counties last year to 70 from 16.

Irish farmers and their minister say Irish cattle herds are among the healthiest in Europe and are protected by strict measures against BSE which include killing an entire herd if one animal is found to be infected.
Exports of Irish cattle to Egypt are worth 180 million punts ($300.2 million) a year.
